governing_objective: Integrate R17 source-backed complete reading with durable terminal process supervision so KCH can prove that it read the mandated sources and followed one owned execution to an exact terminal result without PHL.
reason_for_component_gate_first: The existing commitment monitor only observes PID existence, error substrings and artifact presence. It does not own a process, preserve process identity against PID reuse, capture exit code, emit a canonically sealed terminal receipt, wait without abandoning the commitment, or isolate background-loop failures. A new paired agent benchmark before repairing these defects would test an incomplete mechanism.
implementation_contract: Keep the existing external-PID registration path backward compatible.
Add a shell-free argv launch path through a dedicated worker that persists stdout, stderr and a canonical terminal receipt independently of the KCH runtime lifecycle.
Persist an OS-derived process creation token and reject PID reuse as process identity loss.
Distinguish monitoring, successful terminal completion, nonzero terminal completion, invalid terminal evidence, and terminated-without-evidence.
Expose bounded wait-to-terminal behavior that never kills or relaunches the process on timeout.
Make the background loop isolate and persist per-commitment reconciliation errors instead of dying silently.
Expose launch, wait and evidence through Super-MCP and keep authority, execution and outcome distinct.
Do not execute PHL, access credentials, modify external hosts or claim production readiness.
adjudication_rule: Every gate is PASS, FAIL or NOT_ESTIMABLE. An exit-zero probe does not validate general monitoring efficacy; a timeout is not a terminal process result; artifact presence never substitutes exit code; self-hash integrity never substitutes factual source verification; no global winner is defined in this component gate.
next_gate_if_pass: Run a fresh paired Luna task benchmark using sparse prompts, with KCH forbidden in baseline and automatically bound in the KCH arm, combining ordered multi-file reading and owned terminal supervision.
